title: As-Built Completion and House Registration on Land Certificate 2026
desc: After building: documents and steps to register a house on the land use right certificate under the Land Law 2024, Decree 101/2024 and Decree 207/2026.
summary: The documents needed after construction to complete as-built procedures and register house ownership on the land use right certificate (sổ đỏ) under the new rules.
body: "As-built completion" (hoàn công) is the common term for completing the procedures after building a house so that ownership of the house is recorded on the land use right certificate (sổ đỏ, sổ hồng). Current law calls this registration of assets attached to land.

Under Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP, the homeowner organizes construction and supervision and is responsible for safety; the law encourages homeowners to prepare and keep project records. Keep: the building permit, approved drawings, construction contract, acceptance records and invoices for main materials. For houses of 7 floors or more, or with 2 or more basements, construction and supervision must follow Decree 207/2026 in full.

Under Article 148 of the Land Law 2024, households and individuals have house ownership certified when they hold one of the listed documents, the most common being the residential building permit (where a permit was required). Other documents include a valid sale, gift or inheritance contract for the house, court judgments and decisions, etc.

If the land already has a certificate: carry out the registration of changes to add the house to the certificate. The application under Article 29 of Decree 101/2024/ND-CP includes the registration of changes form (Form No. 11/ĐK), the issued certificate, and documents on the asset (building permit, etc.).
If there is no certificate yet: first-time registration of land and assets, with the application under Article 28 and the procedure under Article 31 and Article 36 of Decree 101/2024/ND-CP.

Under Article 22 of Decree 101/2024/ND-CP: first-time registration of land and assets takes no more than 20 working days, and first-time issuance of the certificate no more than 3 working days; registration of changes has its own time limits by type under the same article.

Building without a permit or contrary to the permit in an area that requires one: the violation must first be handled under Article 25 of Decree 339/2026/ND-CP, and the non-compliant part may not be certified.
A house built on land that is not residential land: the land use purpose must be converted under Article 121 of the Land Law.
Cases where a certificate cannot be issued: see Article 151 of the Land Law.
This article is only a summary for reference and does not replace the legal documents or the guidance of the Land Registration Office where the house is located.
